scenes.tts: One protein can pull an axon toward it, and push another axon away. That protein is netrin, a secreted protein that guides growing axons. Here is a growth cone, the moving tip of a growing axon. Netrin is released from a source on the right, and it thins out with distance. Which way will the growth cone turn?
scenes.visual: Two small growth cones, one drawn toward a netrin dot, one pushed away; then the stage: one growth cone, a netrin source with fading contours, and two question-mark arrows.
scenes.narration: One protein can pull an axon toward it, and push another axon away. That protein is netrin, a secreted protein that guides growing axons. Here is a growth cone, the moving tip of a growing axon. Netrin is released from a source on the right, and it thins out with distance. Which way will the growth cone turn?

scenes.tts: The growth cone reads netrin with receptors on its surface. One receptor is called D C C. A growth cone that carries D C C usually turns toward the netrin source. That is attraction. In the worm, mutants that lack the relative of D C C fail mainly to move toward the cue.
scenes.caption: The growth cone reads netrin with receptors on its surface. One receptor is called DCC. A growth cone that carries DCC usually turns toward the netrin source. That is attraction. In the worm, mutants that lack the relative of DCC fail mainly to move toward the cue.
scenes.visual: Teal cups appear on the growth cone; it curves along a path to the source, leaving an axon trail.
scenes.narration: The growth cone reads netrin with receptors on its surface. One receptor is called DCC. A growth cone that carries DCC usually turns toward the netrin source. That is attraction. In the worm, mutants that lack the relative of DCC fail mainly to move toward the cue.

scenes.tts: Now add a second receptor, called U N C five. A growth cone that carries D C C and U N C five usually turns away from the same netrin. The cue did not change. Only the receptors changed. In worms, forcing U N C five into touch neurons sent their axons away from the cue.
scenes.caption: Now add a second receptor, called UNC5. A growth cone that carries DCC and UNC5 usually turns away from the same netrin. The cue did not change. Only the receptors changed. In worms, forcing UNC5 into touch neurons sent their axons away from the cue.
scenes.visual: Same start; purple cups added beside the teal ones; the growth cone curves away from the source.
scenes.narration: Now add a second receptor, called UNC5. A growth cone that carries DCC and UNC5 usually turns away from the same netrin. The cue did not change. Only the receptors changed. In worms, forcing UNC5 into touch neurons sent their axons away from the cue.

scenes.tts: Receptors are only one layer. The growth cone's inner state is another. To test it, researchers grew single frog spinal growth cones in a dish. A fine pipette puffed netrin on one side, and the growth cones turned toward it. This attraction through D C C needs cyclic A M P signalling. With that signal on, the growth cone turns toward netrin.

scenes.visual: Frog growth cone with teal cups only; orange dots inside it are labelled cyclic AMP; it turns toward the source.
scenes.narration: Receptors are only one layer. The growth cone's inner state is another. To test it, researchers grew single frog spinal growth cones in a dish. A fine pipette puffed netrin on one side, and the growth cones turned toward it. This attraction through DCC needs cyclic AMP signalling. With that signal on, the growth cone turns toward netrin.

scenes.tts: Now block the signal. Use a competing cyclic A M P analogue, or an inhibitor of protein kinase A. The same growth cones turn away from the same pipette. An antibody to D C C stopped both turns. Both turns needed D C C. Blocking cyclic A M P signalling changed the direction.
scenes.caption: Now block the signal. Use a competing cyclic AMP analogue, or an inhibitor of protein kinase A. The same growth cones turn away from the same pipette. An antibody to DCC stopped both turns. Both turns needed DCC. Blocking cyclic AMP signalling changed the direction.
scenes.visual: Orange dots drained and marked blocked; same cone, same teal cups, turns away. Reset; pink antibody caps cover the cups and the cone does not turn.
scenes.narration: Now block the signal. Use a competing cyclic AMP analogue, or an inhibitor of protein kinase A. The same growth cones turn away from the same pipette. An antibody to DCC stopped both turns. Both turns needed DCC. Blocking cyclic AMP signalling changed the direction.

scenes.tts: To predict a turn, ask two questions. Which receptors does the growth cone carry? D C C usually attracts, and U N C five receptors usually add repulsion. And what is its cyclic A M P level? In frog spinal growth cones, lowering it flips attraction to repulsion. Treat this as a starting point, because netrin has other receptors and partners too. Netrin does not decide the turn alone. The receptors and the inner state decide it.
